items.title: NativeHTMLKit developer documentation
items.text:
Illustration only. For real screenshots run the demo gallery in a native desktop and capture them.

Build native HTML/CSS desktop interfaces with familiar Python or PowerShell code. There is no browser engine or embedded JS runtime; a Rust host draws the controls and reports events over local authenticated IPC.

items.title: Start by choosing your path
items.text:
• Python SDK — directly manipulate windows and documents.
  • Python UI — use reactive state and compact components.
  • PowerShell SDK — manage windows and document events from scripts.
  • PowerShell UI — reactive PowerShell components.
  • CLI — native selection, view and form in pipelines.

items.title: Learn by example
items.text: The demo gallery has runnable source files for four entrypoints. Follow the capture guide for screenshots and short clips. Use capability matrices to check what is exposed and in which release.

items.title: Limitations and qualifications
items.text:
• UI version: NativeHTMLKit UI 0.1.0 is a GitHub prerelease; its qualification occurred principally against earlier SDK and Core versions. Revalidate against the exact released current stack before claiming full production support.
  • Python SDK Linux: the currently released x64 wheel uses a manylinux_2_39_x86_64 tag. Earlier glibc versions do not meet that wheel's compatibility floor.
  • PowerShell 5.1: Windows only. Linux uses PowerShell 7.2+.
  • Accessibility: Core 1.0.3 has a reported Linux Orca collapsed-select announcement issue (NHK-CROSS-0010). UI-specific screen-reader coverage remains incomplete.
  • UI reactive state: Python Computed can race when multiple threads mutate dependencies concurrently. Avoid such concurrent patterns until fixed.
  • UI lifecycle: repeated disposed UI windows can accumulate shutdown callbacks; limit repeated create/dispose loops until fixed.
  • Not included: JavaScript/browser APIs, HTTP server, general-purpose plugin framework, UI modal wrapper, web-style routing, video/audio playback, and full Chrome-level HTML/CSS support.
  • Screenshots: initial visual in this documentation is a placeholder illustration; do not treat it as a native test capture. Real screenshots require interactive native qualification and sanitization.

For precise component status see the matrix and linked repository qualifications. A feature appearing in source code is not automatic proof of support on all OS/runtime combinations.

items.title: Architecture — who owns what?
items.text:
flowchart TD
  USER[Python or PowerShell application] --> U[Small UI library, optional]
  USER --> S[Public SDK]
  U --> S
  SHELL[Shell pipeline] --> CLI[Native CLI]
  S --> HOST[Core Rust host]
  CLI --> HOST
  HOST --> NATIVE[Linux KDE Wayland / Windows]

NativeHTMLKit is not a website rendered in a hidden Chromium tab. A Rust native host parses HTML/CSS, handles desktop input and owns native windows. The Python and PowerShell SDKs provide language APIs and manage host transport; the UI library adds a constrained component/state layer, not a second renderer.

Boundary rule: UI libraries may call only their public language SDK; an app may access SDK features not wrapped by UI. A missing native primitive belongs in a separate approved feature for Core/SDK, not a UI-side private RPC hack. The CLI independently implements its own host-v1 client.

Core technical architecture · Python SDK · PowerShell SDK

items.title: Why native instead of Electron or an embedded browser?
items.text:
NativeHTMLKit targets local application development where you want familiar HTML/CSS structure and standard scripting languages without shipping a JavaScript engine, browser process or local web server. Its Rust Core host owns desktop integration and rendering; a Python or PowerShell program owns the logic.

This simplifies some deployment paths but introduces real tradeoffs: the supported HTML/CSS subset is not every browser API, the renderer has its own behavior and compatibility tests, platform-specific input and accessibility need dedicated qualification, and you cannot run arbitrary web JavaScript components. For complex web applications, a browser-based framework may be more appropriate.

Start with the first window, then inspect the capability matrix instead of assuming the full modern web platform exists.
path: Why native instead of Electron or an embedded browser?

items.title: Capture screenshots and short demos
items.text: The landing and Python marketplace README files include a clearly labeled illustration, not a captured UI screenshot. The placeholder PNG is deliberately visible as a temporary onboarding illustration. The deployment bundle includes scripts/media/capture-linux.sh (Wayland/grim), scripts/media/capture-windows.ps1 (interactive Windows session) and scripts/media/make-gif.sh (ffmpeg, if installed).

items.title: Procedure
items.text:
1. Build/install exact published SDK packages on the target desktop. Record OS version, runtime and Core/SDK package versions.
  2. Run examples/python-sdk/gallery.py, examples/powershell-sdk/gallery.ps1, examples/python-ui/gallery.py, examples/powershell-ui/gallery.ps1 separately.
  3. Exercise every visible control. Note any failed/no-op behavior before taking captures. Never claim a demo works just because its source compiles.
  4. Capture the application window. Crop/blur personal data, internal hostnames, tokens, file paths and account names.
  5. Stage a reviewed capture, preserving its identity and original version details:
python3 scripts/media/stage_screenshot.py --source /path/to/capture.png --platform linux --kind python-sdk
python3 scripts/media/stage_screenshot.py --source /path/to/capture.png --platform linux --kind python-sdk --apply --promote --reviewed

--promote updates the public README and (for Python demos) the corresponding marketplace README image. Read the resulting diff before committing. Use --kind powershell-ui or other gallery names as appropriate. Store full capture provenance in assets/README.md. 6. For motion examples, record a short screen capture locally and convert with the included GIF script. Avoid huge looping GIFs in the README; prefer linked short demos.

The GIF workflow is optional; documentation must still make sense in text and with reduced motion enabled.

items.title: Which entry point should I use?
items.text:
Your job Best entry point Why Existing Python app needs a window Python SDK Direct window/document control, small dependency surface Python app needs compact UI controls Python UI State bindings, buttons, inputs, layouts, cards PowerShell administrative script needs desktop input PowerShell SDK Native window lifecycle and OS dialog cmdlets PowerShell script needs a reactive dashboard PowerShell UI Declarative controls and state based on the public SDK Bash/terminal pipeline needs user selection Native CLI Standalone binary, stdin/stdout/exit-status contract

The Python/PowerShell UI libraries are deliberately small, and do not replace SDK access for native dialogs, clipboard, live image surfaces or advanced document operations. Check availability and target OS in the matrix.

items.title: PowerShell UI — state and layout
items.text:
The optional NativeHTMLKit.UI module provides state, computed values, layout and controls using only public NativeHTMLKit SDK cmdlets. The 0.1.0 UI build is a GitHub prerelease: verify Gallery availability and install from the appropriate release package if necessary.

Import-Module NativeHTMLKit.UI -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'Counter'
$ui = New-NHKUi -Title 'Counter' -Theme cobalt -Density compact
$count = New-NHKUiState -Value 0
$null = Add-NHKUiColumn -UI $ui -Content {
  $null = Add-NHKUiText -UI $ui -Bind $count
  $null = Add-NHKUiButton -UI $ui -Text 'Add 1' -Data $count -OnClick {
    param($eventObject,$state) $state.Set([int]$state.Value+1)
  }
}
try {
  $null = Start-NHKUi -UI $ui -Application $app
  Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally {
  Stop-NHKUi -UI $ui
  Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app
}

Use the complete PowerShell UI demo for all simple components, and use PowerShell SDK reference for file dialogs and advanced native actions.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Install-Module NativeHTMLKit -Scope CurrentUser
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit

On Linux use PowerShell 7.2+ with KDE Wayland. Windows supports PowerShell 7.2+ and Windows PowerShell 5.1 in an interactive desktop session.

items.title: Save hello.ps1
items.text:
Import-Module NativeHTMLKit -ErrorAction Stop
$app = Start-NativeHTMLKitScript -Name 'First NativeHTMLKit app'
try {
    $window = New-NativeHTMLKitWindow -Application $app -Title 'Hello'
    $doc = Open-NativeHTMLKitHtml -Window $window -Html '<button id="go">Click me</button><p id="status">Ready</p>'
    $null = Register-NativeHTMLKitDocumentEvent -Document $doc -Type click -Element go -Callback {
        Set-NativeHTMLKitDocumentText -Document $doc -Element status -Text 'Hello from PowerShell!'
    }
    Set-NativeHTMLKitReady -Application $app
    Wait-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app -UntilShutdown
} finally { Close-NativeHTMLKit -Application $app }

Run with pwsh -File hello.ps1 or powershell.exe -File hello.ps1 on Windows. The script is restarted under the native host: keep side effects below Start-NativeHTMLKitScript.

Next: PowerShell SDK gallery · PowerShell UI · SDK reference.

items.title: Python UI — state and controls
items.text:
The optional nativehtmlkit_ui layer is a small reactive UI library built exclusively on the public Python SDK. UI v0.1.0 is a GitHub prerelease; check release/package availability before using uv add nativehtmlkit_ui.

from nativehtmlkit import Application
from nativehtmlkit_ui import UI, state

with Application.start(name="Counter") as app:
    count = state(0)
    ui = UI(title="Counter", theme="cobalt", density="compact")
    with ui.column():
        ui.heading("Native counter")
        ui.text(lambda: f"Count: {count.value}")
        ui.button("+1", on_click=lambda e: count.set(count.value + 1))
    ui.mount(app)
    app.run()

The UI library binds state changes to SDK document updates. Build layouts before ui.mount(app); use ui.post() to deliver worker-thread results to the owning UI thread. There is a known concurrent computed-state issue: see limitations.

For a complete gallery with inputs, conditional regions, select and text lists use Python UI gallery. For native dialogs use the SDK outside the managed component tree.

items.title: Install
items.text:
uv add nativehtmlkit
# alternatively: python -m pip install nativehtmlkit
nativehtmlkit-python doctor

Requires Python 3.10+, a GUI desktop and a wheel for your OS. Linux released wheel glibc floor: 2.39. If installation cannot find a compatible wheel, do not fall back to the host-less source package and expect a GUI to work.

items.title: Save hello.py
items.text:
from nativehtmlkit import Application

def main():
    with Application.start(name="First NativeHTMLKit app") as app:
        window = app.open_html('<main style="padding:24px"><h1>Hello</h1><button id="go">Click me</button><p id="status">Ready</p></main>')
        window.document.on("click", lambda event: window.document.set_text("status", "Hello from Python!"), element="go")
        app.run()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

python hello.py

Click the button: the host sends the event to Python, which updates the displayed document. Application.start() may execute the script twice (supervisor and backend); avoid top-level side effects before it. The alternate python -m nativehtmlkit run module:main accepts a backend main(app) instead.

Next: Interactive Python SDK gallery or Python UI state tutorial. Exact API: Python SDK.

items.title: CLI — native select in a pipeline
items.text:
Download the Linux or Windows x64 executable from the CLI releases. Verify the published SHA256SUMS before execution. The executable is nativehtmlkit (alias nhk where installed).

printf 'alpha
beta
gamma
' | nativehtmlkit select --multi
printf 'name,status
a,up
b,down
' | nativehtmlkit select --input-format csv --multi --output-format json
printf 'one
two
' | nativehtmlkit view
nativehtmlkit doctor

select writes selected records only on success (exit 0), cancel/close uses exit 2, and --timeout uses exit 124. view is read-only. Input is UTF-8 and bounded. For forms, see nativehtmlkit form --html examples/sample-form.html (trusted HTML with <form id="nhk-form">). The CLI is independent of the language SDKs.

See CLI reference for format limits, error codes and lifecycle behavior.
